items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ron Ruben was a fine pianist. Lily, Bruce and myself travelled in Ron's car... I enjoyed every moment that I spent with Bruce Turner and his boys.

ctx.x: my band in exchange for me going there at a later date to work two weeks with an English group. But I was told by the person I had contacted that it was not possible.

So Ron kept knocking on doors and speaking about me until he finally caught the ears of someone that could see his idea in bringing me there. I was so close to the country and many American musicians were going there and transportation from the U.S.A. costed more than it would from France. Eventually I was contacted by a booking agent named Jim Godbolt and we got together on the loot which was no hell after all I had heard about the good bread that was paid in England. But I wanted to get my foot in there at least

In May 1965, I played there for a month and the boss asked me if it would be alright if he engaged the violinist Stuff Smith for 15 days to play as an added attraction with me and my group. Of course, I agreed. I knew Stuff from way back and liked his hard swinging and groovy style. That man could swing like nobody else. Unfortunately, he was in a bad state of health, suffering from stomach ulcers. He was not supposed to drink at all, but couldn't help from having whiskey that he would dilute with plenty of…
